title: In some sense the regenerate fulfil the law
source_text: XII. Porro cum fideles, in quibus gratia divina operatur, dicantur in scriptura Dei mandata servare, dubium non est quin aliquo etiam sensu, dici possint Dei legem implere. Nam Dei mandata sunt idem cum Dei lege. Dei vero mandata servare, & illa eadem implere unum idemque significant. Et certe negari non potest quin vera & sincera charitas, id est, dilectio Dei & proximi, reperiatur in eis qui per spiritum Dei regeniti sunt. Nam qui credunt in Christum, & sunt per spiritum ejus denuo nati, transiverunt a morte ad vitam. Sed, ut testatur Joannes Apostolus, Qui non diligit manet in morte. 1 Joan. 3. Ac perinde quicunque spirituali vita vivunt, necessario Deum & proximum diligunt. Charitas autem est impletio legis, & qui diligit, legem implevit, ut expresse docet Paulus, Rom. 13.
pass_a_gloss: XII. Further, since the faithful, in whom divine grace works, are said in scripture to keep the commandments of God, there is no doubt that in some sense also they can be said to fulfil the law of God. For the commandments of God are the same as the law of God. And to keep the commandments of God, & to fulfil the same, signify one & the same thing. And certainly it cannot be denied that true & sincere charity, that is, love of God & of the neighbour, is found in those who are regenerated by the spirit of God. For those who believe in Christ, & are born again by his spirit, have passed from death to life. But, as John the Apostle testifies, He who does not love abides in death. 1 John 3. And accordingly whoever live by the spiritual life, necessarily love God & their neighbour. But charity is the fulfilling of the law, & he who loves, has fulfilled the law, as Paul expressly teaches, Rom. 13.
pass_b_english: Thesis XII. Since Scripture says that the faithful, in whom God's grace is at work, keep God's commandments, they can no doubt also be said in some sense to fulfil God's law. God's commandments are the same thing as his law, and to keep God's commandments and to fulfil them mean one and the same.

Nor can it be denied that true and sincere charity, the love of God and of one's neighbour, is found in those reborn by God's Spirit. Those who believe in Christ and have been born again by his Spirit have passed from death to life, and, as the apostle John testifies, 'whoever does not love remains in death' (1 John 3).
So all who live the spiritual life necessarily love God and their neighbour. Love is the fulfilment of the law, and whoever loves has fulfilled the law, as Paul expressly teaches in Romans 13.

lemmas.gloss: love of God and of the neighbour
charity is the fulfilling of the law

choices.why: The locus question: whether and how far a person can fulfil the law through Christ's grace.
